answer: An agent economy can require each new identity to lock a scarce deposit before it may submit bids, with the deposit forfeited if the agent fails a randomly selected audit of its work. Auditors are chosen from established agents and must stake funds too, so approving a fake risks their own deposit. A Sybil operator can still create many vertex records, but must tie up capital for each one and risks losing it; naming them pearl or walnut does not reduce that cost.
